description: A team participating in tech-related challenge of Moon and Mars landing zones evaluation and comparison with places on Earth. Currently, the team is already full, not seeking for new members
summary: Our team's project aims to find location on Earth analog to known locations on Mars and Moon and consists of an backend Python app that processed the datasets related to Earth environmental characteristics and compared them to Mars, and a frontend site deployed on Github Pages that provides a visualization for processed data. We believe our project is important because it can highlight which new areas on Earth can be used as a testing grounds for any of the space exploration and landing operations, which is safer(due to the fact you don't have to travel to Moon or Mars to specifically test certain aspects of some technology, equipment) and can bring more scalability, since if there are more places like Moon and Mars on Earth, it brings more testing opportunities.
details:
Out project Earth Analog Finder is a tool that searches the Earth's land surface for places that resemble a chosen location on Mars or the Moon. Current version uses one reference - Jezero crater delta explored by the Perseverance rover. The site is described in code by a JSON profile of measurable criteria grouped into categories such as atmosphere, terrain, geology, thermal and biology, each with a Mars target value, a tolerance, an optional veto threshold and a weight derived from a ranking of the criteria. Mars target values come from orbital data (CTX and MOLA–HRSC elevation models, CRISM mineral maps).

To evaluate Earth data a python pipeline downloads environmental datasets through public APIs, including NASA MODIS land cover, land surface temperature and vegetation index, NASA POWER climate data, the NOAA ETOPO 2022 elevation model, NASADEM / Copernicus 30 m elevation models and NASA EMIT mineral maps. These are resampled onto one global grid of 0.05° cells. For every place on land, the pipeline summarises each criterion over a circle the same size as the Mars reference area, removes places that fail a veto, and scores each criterion between 0 and 1 by its deviation from the Mars target. The most promising areas are then re-measured with finer terrain and mineral data, and the final match is a weighted geometric mean of the criterion scores, reported together with a confidence value and the criterion that limits the match. Quantities that Earth cannot reproduce in absolute terms, such as extreme dryness, are compared as percentiles of Earth's land, and those that cannot be compared at all, such as gravity and air pressure, are listed as limits of the analogy. The results are published as a static website on GitHub Pages, with a world map of candidate areas and a page for each area showing its values, the Mars targets and the deviations.

We think this project can help identify new terrestrial analog sites for testing rovers, instruments and operations procedures before missions, because on Earth it is safer and cheaper than testing on Mars or the Moon, and a larger set of suitable sites gives more testing opportunities in different regions and conditions. Because each profile is a configuration file, other Mars or lunar sites can be added without changing the code.

The backend is written in Python 3.11, using numpy and scipy for computation, rasterio/GDAL, pyhdf and h5py for raster and scientific file formats, earthaccess (NASA Earthdata), pystac-client, jinja2 for page generation. The website uses HTML, CSS, inline SVG and a small optional vanilla JavaScript file, deployed with GitHub Actions to GitHub Pages. The work was organised with GitHub issues and pull requests and specified with GitHub Spec Kit, using Claude Code as an AI(SI) coding assistant. The backend app run was tested on linux laptop with 16 GB RAM without GPUs or external compute.
